ops.title: The kill/reap path proven by TestHostSyncWorkerDeadlineKillsReapsAndReusesLane fails in the wild: it orphaned a daemonkit-worker at 100% CPU for 3 days
ops.premise:
Premise: cc-pool's worker deadline-kill/reap path — the behavior TestHostSyncWorkerDeadlineKillsReapsAndReusesLane exists to prove — can strand a live daemonkit-worker when the supervising process dies uncleanly, contradicting the test's claim.

Field evidence: during the Jul 17-24 swarm incident, the yasyf box carried a daemonkit-worker orphaned at ~100% CPU for ~3 days (observed before the stabilization pass; it had exited on its own by the 2026-07-25 pre-repair sweep, so only the historical observation survives — no live specimen). The 2026-07-25 sweep DID capture the same failure family live in daemonkit and sibling repos: 18 leaked test-helper processes across 5 distinct kill/reap/cancellation/settlement tests, every one carrying trap-''-TERM (evidence: daemonkit cc-notes task 2c931c18, capture file /tmp/daemonkit-test-leaks-1785025196.txt on the box).

Falsifiable questions: (1) does killing the test binary (SIGKILL) mid-TestHostSyncWorkerDeadlineKillsReapsAndReusesLane strand its worker? (2) does the PRODUCTION path (daemon supervising a worker, daemon killed uncleanly) strand the worker, or was the wild orphan strictly a test-context artifact? (3) does daemonkit v0.20.6's next-generation Recover reap such a stranded worker's RECORD while the PROCESS lives on — the exact gap the settlement work did not claim to close?

Note: the affected test's settlement assert was made poll-based in commit bbcc94f (settlement-race sweep) — unrelated to this premise, which is about process stranding, not record timing.

ops.text: Wild observation (pre-stabilization): daemonkit-worker pid 4829 era, ~100% CPU, ~3 days, on the yasyf box during the swarm; gone by 2026-07-25 sweep
Same-family confirmation: 5 kill/reap-proving test families across the fleet strand TERM-immune helpers when the test binary dies uncleanly (daemonkit task 2c931c18)
